# TinyStudio

TinyStudio is the business behind this site, tinystudio.io. Other businesses
share the name — a Mac subtitle app, a fibre-arts magazine, a design agency, a
video production studio, a Los Angeles venue, an unrelated studio LLC. None of
them are this TinyStudio, and this TinyStudio is none of them. The site states no base city or office address.

TinyStudio sells one human-reviewed managed service around the page a
business's revenue depends on: The Website Appraisal, a free leak audit of
high-ticket service homepages, and The Growth Desk that closes what the audit
finds. It is a managed service with human review, not autonomous software.

Canonical URL: https://tinystudio.io/
Contact: hello@tinystudio.io

## Current Offer: The Website Appraisal

The Website Appraisal is a complimentary leak audit, yours to keep whether or
not TinyStudio is ever engaged. It serves high-ticket service businesses —
clinics, surgeons, dentists, spas, property, dealers, brokers and similar —
and clients are never named.

Six audits a month; when the sixth is taken, the intake closes until the
next. Findings arrive inside five working days, and no call is required at
any point.

The audit reads the one page a business's revenue depends on, the way a
customer with intent reads it, in four passes: the money page, the paid
creative, the unanswered pre-purchase questions, and the reach. Each pass is
run by a specialist with one job, then read and signed by a person before it
reaches the client. The result is a short, plain document: each fault named,
in the order it costs the business, with the fix beside it.

## The Growth Desk

If the leaks are to be closed rather than merely found, The Growth Desk runs
at $2,500 a month on a three-month minimum. Month one corrects the costliest
fault: the page rewritten or rebuilt, a dev-ready handoff if the client's own
team ships it, and search-trust basics. Months two and three build the loop
that keeps the standard up: weekly checks, one revision, and tracking that
says whether the fix held.

There is one promise about outcomes, and only one: the delivery guarantee. If
the month-one deliverables are not in the client's hands within fourteen
working days of Day 0, month one is refunded in full. Day 0 begins only once
payment, access, the approval owner and the implementation owner are
recorded, and the clock pauses if TinyStudio is waiting on the client.

## How The Work Runs

Seven specialist agents do the research, drafting and checking, each with a
single job, a fixed set of inputs and a checklist it must satisfy, working
from the client's own pages and numbers — never a template for the sector. A
person reviews fit, every claim, all client-facing work, delivery and
renewal, and signs every audit. Automation may prepare research, drafts, QA,
packages and routing, but never autonomously sends, publishes, spends,
approves, accepts or renews.

## Evidence

The site's finding is backed by market research that TinyStudio shares freely:
an automated read of served homepage HTML, refreshed daily. The current set
covers 99 sites across thirteen industries and eight geographies; 89 are
readable and ten are blocked by bot protection and excluded from every count.
Of the 89 readable, 53 answer none of the questions a buyer asks before
committing, and 57 show no price. Inner pages are deliberately not counted.
This number is today's and changes as the set is re-read.

## Not Promised

There are no revenue, ranking, ROAS, conversion, booked-call, or sales-volume
guarantees. The delivery guarantee is a promise about the work, not the
market. Client work is never published: no logos, no case studies, no
testimonials, no "as seen at".

## Data Handling

The public app stores email signup and lightweight usage metadata in
Cloudflare D1, including daily rate-limit counters and a daily IP-derived
rate-limit key. Submitted business context is processed to generate output
and is not stored by this app.

There is no public endpoint for reading collected emails or usage metadata.
Client-side code does not call model providers, platform admin APIs, ad
accounts, databases, or private credentials directly.

## Legacy Self-Serve Agent Desk

The earlier self-serve Agent Desk, which generated a one-shot Pipeline Brief,
is demoted and is not the current offer. Agent Desk surfaces still reachable
on this site are legacy, not the current offer. The legacy surface keeps its
safety rails:

- No campaign publishing
- No ad spend changes
- No ad account connection
- No prospect message sending
- Client-side code does not call model providers, platform admin APIs, ad accounts, databases, or private credentials directly.
